\newcommand{\anchorParagraph}{We registered anchor criteria before any anchor run (protocol 4.7): no configuration may beat the physical floor (A1); on an A100 x86 host the median error must be at most 25\% (A2) and the model must under-predict at least two thirds of the configurations, as on the A10 (A3). The predictor is the third-party fit with each machine's STREAM Triad and datasheet GPU bandwidth; each prediction file was committed by the job before the one that measured. No A100 had capacity during the study, so the registered A100 test is still open. On a GH200 (72-core Grace, LPDDR5X, NVLink-C2C; Triad 301\,GB/s), a platform outside the fitted envelope, 29 \texttt{--n-cpu-moe} configurations of six GGUF files (Mixtral-8x7B at Q4\_K\_M and Q8\_0; Phi-3.5-MoE, Qwen2-57B-A14B and Qwen3-30B-A3B at Q4\_K\_M; DeepSeek-V2-Lite at Q8\_0) show two regimes. With experts on the CPU (25 configurations) the model under-predicts 20 of them, measured/predicted 0.55--1.50 (median error 23\%), the conservative direction seen on the A10. All-GPU runs (4) are over-predicted, measured/predicted 0.28--0.92: at 4\,TB/s a small model's decode step is dominated by per-layer fixed costs that Eq.~(1) omits. Over all 29, the median error is 24\%; no configuration exceeds the physical floor (the closest reaches 86\% of it), and time per token is affine in the CPU layers ($R^2\ge0.997$). The audited rows sit in the offloaded regime, where the model errs on the side of calling baselines strong.}
